arabian-nights-burton-supplemental-1886-.creator: Richard F. Burton (trans.)
arabian-nights-burton-supplemental-1886-.description: Vol. 6 of Burton's Supplemental Nights (1886-88) — Aladdin, Ali Baba and the further tales completing his unexpurgated Arabian Nights. Public domain. Sourced from Project Gutenberg ebook #3450 (https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/3450).

arxiv-1805-11795.title: Interference of the signal from a local dynamical process with the quantum state propagation in spin chains
arxiv-1805-11795.creator: Saikat Sur, V. Subrahmanyam
arxiv-1805-11795.description: Abstract The effect of a local instantaneous quantum dynamical process (QDP), either unitary or non-unitary, on the quantum state transfer through a unitary Hamiltonian evolution is investigated for both integrable and non-integrable dynamics. There are interference effects of the quantum state propagation and the QDP signal propagation.

arxiv-2202-13407.title: Average shadowing and gluing property
arxiv-2202-13407.creator: Michael Blank
arxiv-2202-13407.description: Abstract The purpose of this work is threefold: (i) extend shadowing theory for discontinuous and non-invertible systems, (ii) consider more general classes of perturbations (for example, small only on average), (iii) establish a general theory based on the property that the shadowing holds for the case of a single perturbation.

arxiv-2205-08840.title: REDISCUSSION OF ECLIPSING BINARIES. PAPER IX.
arxiv-2205-08840.creator: THE SOLAR-TYPE SYSTEM KIC 5359678
arxiv-2205-08840.description: Abstract By John Southworth Astrophysics Group, Keele University, Staffordshire, ST5 5BG, UK KIC 5359678 is a 6.231-d period F-type eclipsing binary system whose component stars both show starspot activity. It was observed by the Kepler satellite in long cadence for the full four-year duration of the mission. Wang et al.

arxiv-2209-12528.title: Dordis: Efficient Federated Learning with Dropout-Resilient Differential Privacy Conference: Nineteenth European Conference on Computer Systems; April 22–25, 2024; Athens, Greece Nineteenth European Conference on Computer Systems (EuroSys ’24), April 22–25, 2024, Athens, Greece Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.
arxiv-2209-12528.creator: Zhifeng Jiang, Wei Wang, Ruichuan Chen
arxiv-2209-12528.description: Abstract . Federated learning (FL) is increasingly deployed among multiple clients to train a shared model over decentralized data. To address privacy concerns, FL systems need to safeguard the clients’ data from disclosure during training and control data leakage through trained models when exposed to untrusted domains.

arxiv-2305-16226.title: Linear Ultrastrong Optomechanical Interaction
arxiv-2305-16226.creator: Kahan Dare, Jannek J. Hansen, Iurie Coroli, Aisling Johnson, Markus Aspelmeyer, Uroš Delić
arxiv-2305-16226.description: Abstract Light-matter interaction in the ultrastrong coupling regime can be used to generate exotic ground states with two-mode squeezing and may be of use for quantum enhanced sensing. Current demonstrations of ultrastrong coupling have been performed in fundamentally nonlinear systems.

arxiv-2308-12999.title: Anomaly Enforced Gaplessness and Symmetry Fractionalization for S ​ p ​ i ​ n G Spin_{G} Symmetries
arxiv-2308-12999.creator: T. Daniel Brennan
arxiv-2308-12999.description: Abstract Symmetries and their anomalies give strong constraints on renormalization group (RG) flows of quantum field theories. Recently, the identification of a theory’s global symmetries with its topological sector has provided additional constraints on RG flows to symmetry preserving gapped phases due to mathematical results in category and topological quantum field theory.

arxiv-2309-05183.title: Data Summarization beyond Monotonicity: Non-monotone Two-Stage Submodular Maximization
arxiv-2309-05183.creator: Shaojie Tang
arxiv-2309-05183.description: Abstract The objective of a two-stage submodular maximization problem is to reduce the ground set using provided training functions that are submodular, with the aim of ensuring that optimizing new objective functions over the reduced ground set yields results comparable to those obtained over the original ground set. This problem has applications in various domains including data summarization.

arxiv-2405-02628.title: Contrastive Dual-Interaction Graph Neural Network for Molecular Property Prediction
arxiv-2405-02628.creator: Zexing Zhao, Guangsi Shi, Xiaopeng Wu, Ruohua Ren, Xiaojun Gao, Fuyi Li
arxiv-2405-02628.description: Abstract Molecular property prediction is a pivotal component in the realm of AI-driven drug discovery and molecular representation learning. Despite recent progress, existing methods struggle with challenges such as limited generalization capabilities and inadequate representation learning from unlabeled data, particularly in tasks specific to molecular structures.

arxiv-2508-05456.title: Weak interaction rates of s ​ d sd -shell Urca pairs in stellar environment using a shell-model approach
arxiv-2508-05456.creator: Shweta Sharma, Praveen C. Srivastava, Toshio Suzuki
arxiv-2508-05456.description: Abstract In this work, the weak interaction rates of s ​ d sd -shell nuclei in the hot and dense stellar environment are calculated using the shell model. The ab initio effective interactions are employed for the calculation of Gamow-Teller strengths and weak rates in addition to the phenomenological interaction.

arxiv-2510-03963.title: Weyl-invariant subspaces are (usually) not generic
arxiv-2510-03963.creator: Riku Kurama, Ruoxi Li, Henry Talbott, and Rachel Webb
arxiv-2510-03963.description: Abstract . Let V V be a linear representation of a connected complex reductive group G G . Given a choice of character θ \theta of G G , Geometric Invariant Theory defines a locus V θ s ​ s ​ ( G ) ⊆ V V^{ss}_{\theta}(G)\subseteq V of semistable points.

arxiv-2605-15275.creator: Daniel R. Piacitelli, Alyson M. Brooks, N. Nicole Sanchez, Hetvi Khatri, Charlotte Christensen, Cameron Hummels, Nishant Mishra, Akaxia Cruz, Ben Keller, Thomas R. Quinn, Sijing Shen, James Wadsley

arxiv-2606-21370.title: Computationally guided modifications of Cvi UPO to improve catalytic activity
arxiv-2606-21370.creator: Hanna-Friederike Poggemann, Tim Dirks, Timo Jacob, Christoph Jung

pmc-11353674.title: Correlational Insights into Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in Lebanon
pmc-11353674.creator: Melyssa Assaf, Melissa Rouphael, Sarah Bou Sader Nehme, Michel Soufia, Abbas Alameddine, Souheil Hallit, Marc Landry, Tania Bitar, Walid Hleihel, Paul B Tchounwou
pmc-11353674.description: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), a prevalent childhood neurodevelopmental disorder with complex etiology involving genetic and environmental factors, causes impairments across various life domains and substantial social and economic burden. Identifying correlates to prevent its onset and decrease its incidence is crucial.

pmc-11397292.title: Energy Balance and Dietary Intake in Young Rugby Players during a Pre-Season Micro-Cycle: A Cluster Analysis
pmc-11397292.creator: Maher Souabni, Giovanna C Del Sordo, Freddy Maso, Paul Peyrel, Clément Maviel, Fabrice Vercruyssen, Pascale Duché, Oussama Saidi, Lewis Anthony Gough
pmc-11397292.description: Rugby players must develop excellent levels of conditioning during adolescence. However, this pivotal period of life is also characterized by a surge in biological growth, which further increases the energy and nutritional requirements of this population. This study examined within-individual differences in energy intake (EI) and energy balance (EB) of 46 young rugby players during a pre-season micro-cycle.

pmc-11454766.title: 7201 Association of Chronotype and Glycemic Control Among Patients with Diabetes Mellitus: A Single Center Study
pmc-11454766.creator: Noemi Angela D Nunez, Oliver Allan C Dampil, Albert Macaire C Ong Lopez
pmc-11454766.description: Disclosure: N.D. Nunez: None. O.C. Dampil: None. A.C. Ong Lopez: None.Chronotype preference is an emerging risk factor to the development of diabetes mellitus and poor glycemic outcomes. This study aims to determine the association of chronotype based on the Munich Chronotype questionnaire among patients with diabetes mellitus and their level of glycemic control.

pmc-11651132.title: Efficacy of Preemptive Topical Lidocaine 5% Plaster in the Prevention of Post-Craniotomy Pain, a Randomized Clinical Trial
pmc-11651132.creator: Xueye Han, Yixuan Yang, Tong Ren, Nan Ji, Fang Luo
pmc-11651132.description: ObjectiveThe current landscape is characterized by a dearth of effective, safe, simple, and noninvasive methods for preventing pain following craniotomy. This clinical trial seeks to evaluate the efficacy profile of preemptive application of a topical 5% lidocaine patch in alleviating post-craniotomy pain.MethodsThis was a multi-centric, prospective randomized placebo-controlled triple-blind clinical trial.

pmc-11690904.title: THE INFLUENCE OF THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC ON DOMESTIC ELDER ABUSE IN JAPAN
pmc-11690904.creator: Tadashi Wada, Hitoshi Suda, Tamiko Uehara, Kana Sato
pmc-11690904.description: We are very interested in the influence of COVID-19 pandemic on elder abuse, especially its effects on the incidence. We investigated its incidence per population of validated domestic elder abuse cases in Matsudo City, Chiba, Japan, and in all over Japan.

pmc-12574625.title: Predictors of Decannulation Success in Tracheostomy: A 10‐Year Analysis of the Global Tracheostomy Collaborative Database
pmc-12574625.creator: Charissa J. Zaga, Carly E. Milliren, Brendan A. McGrath, Christina J. Yang, Bradley A. Schiff, Stephen J. Warrillow, Jennifer K. Henningfeld, Prudence A. Gregson, Joshua R. Bedwell, Karen M. Beaudet, Michael J. Brenner, Vinciya Pandian
pmc-12574625.description: ObjectiveDecannulation is a critical milestone in functional recovery after tracheostomy, but standardized guidelines are lacking. This study examined factors associated with tracheostomy decannulation success, comparing hospital utilization, adverse events, and survival outcomes between decannulated and non‐decannulated patients.Study DesignRetrospective, observational study.

pmc-12577057.title: Should whole body vibration be used for falls prevention in older people living in the community?
pmc-12577057.creator: Suzanne M Dyer, Wing S Kwok, Rik Dawson, Ian D Cameron, Catherine Sherrington
pmc-12577057.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The Canadian Task Force on Preventive Health Care has recently published a systematic review and network meta-analysis that concludes that whole-body vibration (WBV) has moderate-certainty evidence for falls prevention for older people living in the community.

pmc-12622784.title: A molecular toolbox to modulate gene expression and protein secretion in the bacterial predator Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus
pmc-12622784.creator: Ljiljana Mihajlovic, Lara M. Hofacker, Florian Lindner, Priyanikha Jayakumar, Andreas Diepold, Simona G. Huwiler, Danielle A. Garsin, Kai Papenfort, Danielle A. Garsin, Kai Papenfort, Danielle A. Garsin, Kai Papenfort
pmc-12622784.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The predatory bacterium Bdellovibrio bacteriovorus kills and consumes other bacteria, thrives in diverse environments and holds great potential to address major challenges in medicine, agriculture, and biotechnology. As a bacterial predator it represents an alternative to traditional antimicrobial strategies to combat multidrug-resistant bacterial pathogens and prevent food waste, while the multitude of predatory enzymes it produces have potential for biotechnological applications.

pmc-12700462.title: Drug-related stigma among people who inject drugs – development and validation of the drug use stigma scale (DUSS)
pmc-12700462.creator: Robin A. Pollini, Catherine E. Paquette, Brandon Irvin, Jennifer L. Syvertsen, Christa L. Lilly
pmc-12700462.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Drug use is a highly stigmatized behavior, and drug-related stigma is a key driver of behavioral risk, lower health care utilization, and associated adverse health outcomes among people who inject drugs (PWID). While instruments exist for measuring drug-related stigma, their applicability to community-based PWID across multiple stigma types (enacted, anticipated, internalized) and settings (health care, society, family) is limited, as most were developed using treatment-based samples and all were developed in urban populations.

pmc-12705744.title: Crossing borders securely: synthetic data and federated networks for privacy-preserving access to real-world data and emerging use cases
pmc-12705744.creator: Echo H Wang, Puja Myles, Randi Foraker, Sengwee Toh, Lucy Mosquera, Khaled El Emam, Mehmet Burcu
pmc-12705744.description: The demand for demographically and geographically diverse, high-quality, fit-for-purpose real-world data has been increasing to support regulatory and other healthcare decision making. Accessing and sharing healthcare data across sites, regions, and countries while ensuring data privacy has been a long-standing challenge.

pmc-13435897.title: Characterization of Klebsiella phages PMBT12, PMBT63, and PMBT64 with functional insights into a Hoc-like, mucin-interacting protein of phage PMBT63
pmc-13435897.creator: Anna Ewertz, Erik Brinks, Gyu-Sung Cho, Frank Hille, Charles M. A. P. Franz
pmc-13435897.description: Three novel Klebsiella phages, PMBT12, PMBT63, and PMBT64, were isolated and characterized. The phages revealed distinct morphologies, phylogenetic backgrounds, and a high degree of genomic divergence. PMBT12 and PMBT64 exhibited narrow host ranges, whereas PMBT63 demonstrated a broader host range across the tested Klebsiella strains with diverse sequence and capsule types.

pmc-13579519.title: Effects of a carboxymethyl fenugreek polysaccharide/sodium carboxymethyl cellulose composite binder on the physicochemical properties and sensory quality of reconstituted tobacco leaves
pmc-13579519.creator: Huayu Li, Lin Jiang, Hongtao Xu, Shaohui Yan, Ling Chang, Xiaoyu Li, Mengmeng Zu, Xiaopeng Yang, Xiaoming Ji
pmc-13579519.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Reconstituted tobacco leaves (RTLs) are widely used in heat-not-burn products, but single-component binders can limit their sheet integrity and sensory quality. Here, carboxymethyl fenugreek polysaccharide (CFP) was blended with sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) at CFP : CMC mass ratios of 0 : 10, 1 : 9, 3 : 7, 5 : 5 and 10 : 0 and evaluated in thick-slurry RTLs.
